name: Synth strings, ensemble and choir layers
goal: Build string-section and choir-like synth layers: PWM 80s strings, unison with delayed vibrato, saw/FM blends, opposite-direction arpeggiated plucks that read as strings, noise-comb ensemble pads and hybrid choir pads.

sources.title: The Secret to HUGE Dark Vocal Pads in Serum 2
How to Design Cinematic Realistic String Pads - Zebra 3 Sound Design Tutorial
How To Synth 5: Synthetic Ambient Orchestraish Strings
80s String Pad Tutorial (1/2) - Pulse Width Modulation in Tyrell N6
How To Make A Cinematic String Section - Sound Design Tutorial

theory: Ensemble = many slightly detuned, slightly late voices; delayed vibrato (5-6 Hz after ~0.3 s) and slow attacks mimic bowing; PWM produces chorus-like motion from one oscillator.
prerequisites: A reverb with pitch-shift (shimmer) and modulation, or a reverb plus pitch shifter
A synth with saw/additive oscillators, filter envelope, vibrato, unison and an arpeggiator
FX: frequency-shift/blur widener, chorus/dimension, ping-pong delay, high-passed distortion, comb, reverb, EQ
Reverb, mod/diffusion effect, EQ with resonator mode or a resonator, compressor
Sub and noise oscillators, two filters incl. notch

Synth with comb filters fed by noise (static/white and pink noise types), LFOs, key tracking and global FX (Zebra 3 used in the source), or Web Audio: two noise sources into per-voice tuned feedback delay combs (implementation note)
Synth with ≥2 oscillators, unison with detune, osc FM from another osc, filter with drive, 2 envelopes, 2 LFOs with LFO→LFO-rate routing, FX (EQ, reverb, delay, distortion), macros
Two-oscillator subtractive synth with pulse wave + PW modulation (or Web Audio PeriodicWave/pulse via two offset saws)
Volume automation and a sidechain ducker

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: Rendered part or recipe following the workflow

constraints: Portable recipe; not affiliated with any vendor; do not copy factory presets or sample packs.
Numbers in variants come from the source video transcripts; workflow steps are the consolidated mainstream practice.
Bring drums in early and avoid pitch wobble unless asked (user preferences from daily tests).

steps.action: Oscillators: PWM pulse with free-running LFO (0.3-1 Hz), or 2 saws + unison, optional low FM for bite.
Attack 0.1-0.5 s, release 0.5-1.5 s; vibrato 5-6 Hz delayed ~0.3 s, depth a few cents.
Filter LP 2-5 kHz with velocity/brassy filter envelope for swells.
Voice the parts like a section: low strings root/fifth, violins in thirds/sixths above, keep voice-leading smooth.
Arp trick: two plucky saw arpeggios in opposite directions blur into a string texture under reverb.
Choir: formant/vocal tables or noise-comb lanes for highs, synthetic lows underneath; notch harsh bands.
Add ensemble/chorus and hall reverb; high-pass under 150 Hz.
Hear the theory: run `/home/box/audio-tools/bin/python sample-lab/theory/detune_unison.py` from the repo root and compare the sections; reuse its functions as a starting point for renders.
steps.expect: WAV in sample-lab/theory/out/ demonstrating the principle

verification: Render a short test and A/B against a reference at matched loudness
Run the generator and confirm it writes a WAV without error
Check mono compatibility and that no element masks the kick/bass

variants.name: Dark hybrid vocal pad: choir-like wavetable plus an octave-up choir sample FM'd in (~34%), with sub and a little noise. Lows/mids are low-passed while the natural sample keeps the highs, a subtle LFO notch moves the mids, and one slow rising ramp drives the FX
variants.goal: Build a dark, haunting vocal pad for intros, breakdowns or tension layers by blending a real choir sample with synthetic layers that sound vocal. Osc A: a choir-type wavetable with chorus-like unison and its position moved by a single slow, rising ramp (one main movement). Osc B: a choir multisample an octave up with light tube saturation, frequency-modulating A at ~34% for grit. Add a default sub (choir has little sub) and very low white noise (or hum) for full-spectrum air. Route A + sub through a low-pass, but keep B (natural) out of it so the high end comes from the real voice. Then all go into filter 2, a subtle notch (~18%) whose amount and cutoff move on the LFO for mid-range expression. FX: a blended, very wide frequency-shifter/blur stereo layer (mix ~half), dimension ~6%, hyper-chorus automated up to ~32% at the top of the ramp, ping-pong delay ~10–11%, distortion only above ~300 Hz, a little comb, reverb ~10%, then a high-end presence boost. Delta vs our pad skills: natural-highs / synthetic-lows routing and the single-ramp FX bloom on a vocal pad.
steps: Osc A: choir-like wavetable, unison for chorus, slight low-pass. Create one main modulator, a slow triangle that effectively ramps up, on wavetable position (and later FX amounts).
Osc B: choir multisample an octave higher with a bit of tube saturation, defaults otherwise. FM it into osc A at ~34% for a touch of grit.
Add a sub oscillator at default level under everything, and white noise (or hum) at a very low level for full-spectrum air.
Filter 1: low-pass on osc A + sub only; route osc B around it so the natural choir provides the high end.
Filter 2 on the combined signal: notch at ~18% mix (100% shows the full effect), with the amount rising on the LFO and the cutoff moving slightly too, for mid-range expression and cohesion.

FX 1: a frequency-shifter/blur stereo layer, mix ~half, blur ~half, shift and range lowered, blended in as a moving super-wide layer. Dimension ~6%. Hyper-chorus automated from low up to ~32% at the top of the ramp.
FX 2: ping-pong delay ~10–11%; distortion with a high-pass so only ~300 Hz upward is saturated; a little comb filter (macro candidate); reverb ~10%; final high-shelf presence boost.

variants.name: Cinematic ensemble string pad from noise-excited combs: two comb lanes (static vs pink noise, different comb flavours) with fast random pitch drift for a section feel, key-tracked low-pass so low notes stop sounding metallic, a smoothed saw layer and an EQ'd sine/FM low end, a low-boosting resonator, mod-wheel cutoff, velocity that shortens attack and release, a tiny strike pitch envelope and offset triangle 'bow' LFOs on comb tilt
variants.goal: Build a realistic, wide sustained string pad (not a solo bowed voice) on comb filters. Lane A: static noise with a slow attack and slow release into a comb whose feedback is raised until sharp, low-passed to take the edge off, with a fast random (non-synced) ramp LFO on fine detune so it behaves like many players. Lane B: pink noise (more warmth and body) into a different comb flavour, also detuned. Mix both lanes and control them through one filter with cutoff key-tracked (centre near middle E, about 64 in the middle) so higher keys stay bright and low keys are darker and less metallic; add a little comb distortion. Add body with a smoothed saw (curve filter in string range, doubled for width) and a sine/FM layer EQ'd to low end only. Global FX: subtle mod/diffusion (slow shape), reverb, an EQ resonator mode boosting lows on lane 2, light peak compression. Make it playable: mod wheel → cutoff, velocity → shorter attack and shorter release (never zero), a tiny curved pitch rise on strike applied to both comb pitches, and triangle LFOs at different second-based rates on comb tilt/flavour (not 'structure', which changes pitch). Distinct from today's MPE bowed-string skill: an ensemble pad with drift, dual-lane flavours and velocity/LFO articulation.
steps: Lane A: static noise → amp envelope with slow attack and slow release → comb. Raise comb feedback until the tone is sharp and pitched; low-pass the noise to remove edge.
Add an LFO set to random ramp, not tempo-synced, routed lightly to fine detune; speed it up until it reads as a group of players, stopping short of vibrato.
Global FX: a little mod/diffusion (slow shape), reverb; set a non-resonant 6 dB linear filter as a starting point and increase width.
Lane B: duplicate the idea with pink noise into a different comb flavour/complexity, detuned the same way. Mix lanes A and B and route both through one shared filter.
Key-track the shared filter cutoff with the centre near middle E (about 64 in the middle). Add a little comb distortion if wanted.

Body: add a saw oscillator smoothed with a curve filter in string range (double it for width) and a sine/FM layer EQ'd to keep only low end. Optionally add an EQ resonator boosting lows on lane 2 in the global FX.
Playability: mod wheel → filter cutoff; velocity → attack and release so harder strikes get shorter attack and shorter release (keep a minimum above zero); compress only the top peaks.

Strike pitch: a short curved envelope adding a tiny pitch rise to both comb pitches (exaggerate to hear, then reduce). Bow motion: triangle LFOs with rates in seconds on comb tilt/flavour, at different rates per lane so they do not move in unison.

variants.name: Make synth layers read as strings or orchestra by obscuring them: two saw-based arpeggiated plucks moving in opposite directions, a fast-open filter envelope and vibrato, a shared pitch-shifting modulated reverb, and level automation plus sidechain so the listener only hears brief glimpses without context
variants.goal: Imply acoustic strings with simple synthesis plus psychoacoustics. Harmonic content: saw-like spectra (strings and brass are close to a saw series). Layer two arpeggiators playing the same chords: one rising, one reversed so they cross; double the arp step time (half speed); each voice uses a brass-like filter envelope (opens fast, decays: a smoothed pluck), light unison, real vibrato, and a spectral/frequency-mode phaser masked to act above the fundamental so the note pitch stays clean; the second voice has a longer pluck, darker filter and more unison. Arp cycle length depends on chord note count, so voice chords deliberately. Send both to one shared reverb with large size and diffusion, low feedback, a downward pitch shimmer and high modulation depth. Then automate the layer's level by feel so it only comes through at chosen moments, and sidechain it under the drums; a supporting soft chord stack gets a big reverb with a gate so tails don't run on. The brain fills in an orchestra because it never hears the sound's before/after context.
steps: Program the chords with a fixed note count (e.g. 3 notes) so arp cycles stay predictable; arp cycle length grows with note count.
Voice 1: saw-like oscillator, light unison, vibrato on, filter envelope that opens fast then decays (brass-style smoothed pluck), arpeggiator going up at half speed (double the default step time).
Add a phaser (or harmonic pitch modulation) masked so it only affects partials above the fundamental, so pitch stays clean while upper harmonics shimmer.
Voice 2: same idea with a longer pluck decay, lower filter, a bit more unison, arp direction reversed (starts at the top) so the two layers cross.
Send both voices to one shared reverb: large size and diffusion, low feedback, pitch shift down in the feedback, high modulation depth; high-pass and lift the top before the reverb.
Automate the layer's level by feel so it only comes through at selected moments, and sidechain it under the drums.
Optional support: a soft sustained chord stack with big reverb, gated so tails stop when the chord stops, with a fader dip so it starts large and smooths out.

variants.name: 80s PWM string pad: pulse wave with free-running (seconds-based) LFO on pulse width, slight osc-2 detune, slow attack/release, static filter
variants.goal: Build a classic 1980s string pad from an init patch: switch the oscillator from saw to pulse, modulate pulse width from an LFO set in seconds (free-running, ~0.7, not tempo-synced so the ensemble rate never changes with song tempo), blend a second oscillator ever so slightly detuned, low-pass to remove the very high end with the filter envelope and other filter mod sources switched off, slow fade-in attack and long release — a dedicated PWM string pad distinct from our PW drone and unison string-section skills.
steps: Start from an init patch; keep a scope visible. Change oscillator 1 from saw to pulse (square = 50% duty cycle; pulse widths roughly 10–90% duty).
Route an LFO to pulse width and watch the scope: the pulse width sweeps.
Switch the PW LFO from tempo-sync to free-running seconds so the string movement keeps the same rate regardless of DAW tempo; set ~0.7 and a moderate depth.
Bring in oscillator 2 (presenter's level ~17.5) alongside osc 1, then detune osc 2 ever so slightly (fine ~0.20) — perfectly in-tune oscillators lose the effect.
Lower the low-pass cutoff to cut the really high end; reduce output level if hot.
Amp envelope: much slower attack (presenter ~38 display units) for a fade-in and a long release that tails naturally.
Set master transpose from −12 to 0 so A440 plays A440. Turn off the filter envelope and other filter modulation sources so the filter stays static.
Set the voice/unison count the presenter uses (2), play chords to confirm the 1980s string pad, and save it as a patch.

variants.name: Synth string section: 7-voice unison saw, subtle bow-brightness envelope, LFO-on-detune vibrato with ramped rate, low FM blend
variants.goal: Build a light cinematic string section from saws: 7-voice unison saw (~7% detune) into a low-resonance 12/6 dB low-pass ~400–450 Hz with a little drive, slow amp envelope (A ~1.5 s, D ~5 s, S ~70%, R ~2 s, full velocity), a subtle filter envelope (+15% range) for bowing brightness, ensemble vibrato by LFO-modulating unison detune (1 s, small amount) whose rate is swept by a second ramp LFO, a second 7-voice osc FM'd by the first at ~30–35%, then low-cut, gentle top cut, big reverb, quiet quarter-note delay, and 20–30% soft clip on macros.
steps: Init patch. Osc1 saw, 7 unison voices, ~7% detune; set the two osc start controls the video zeroes (unnamed in the transcript; typically phase/random-phase) to 0 to avoid clicks and pops. Route through filter 1: analog low-pass 12 dB/oct (6 dB works even better), resonance 0, cutoff ~450 Hz (later ~400 Hz), a little drive.
Amp envelope: attack ~1.5 s, decay ~5 s, sustain ~70%, release ~2 s. Velocity sensitivity 100%; polyphony ~24 voices so notes don't cut each other off.
Bowing brightness: envelope 2 attack ~0.5–0.6 s (rounded curve), decay ~4–5 s, sustain ~20–30%, release ~0.1 s → filter cutoff with a small amount (~15). Keep it subtle.
Ensemble vibrato: LFO1 at 1 s period → unison detune amount ~0.06 (detune moves roughly 7% → 10–11% and back) rather than modulating global pitch.
Variable vibrato speed: LFO2 as a ramp, 4–5 s period → LFO1 rate (amount ~0.2) via the mod matrix so vibrato starts slow and speeds up, then resets.
Second osc: 7 unison voices ~10% detune through filter 1, FM from osc1 at a low amount (~30–35%; high amounts sound bad).

FX: low-cut rumble (keep lows only for bass use), take a little off the top to reduce fizz, reverb with high mix and large size (decay up to 4–5 s), quarter-note mono delay with low feedback and low mix, soft-clip distortion with drive up and mix ~20–30% (end of chain, or before reverb so the reverb carries the grit).
Macros: one macro → distortion drive, one → reverb mix, and one macro to several FX at once (reverb + delay) for quick performance control.
